architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk

voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

planner.failure_mode: viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence, with unresolved contribution from modifier chemistry versus reactive-core dilution
planner.failure_mode_evidence: At 120 C, the original E5 formulation increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 minutes, compared with 9.51% for E1 over the same window; the measured 15 to 90 minute changes were 93.08% and 16.85%, respectively.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local hold data contain only one original run each for E1 and E5, with four time points over 15 to 90 minutes and no measured modifier-axis coverage sufficient to distinguish linear dilution, superlinear resin suppression, and tackifier-specific effects. The existing temperature sweeps have six points over 80 to 130 C across several E2 repeats, whereas the time-dependent behavior is sparsely sampled across chemistry.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity at 120 C at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes and report the matched-window SI_15_60 relative change.
Use at least two independent preparation repeats for each tested composition, with the process history and thermal state recorded.
Compare an acrylic-only composition and a composition with a nonzero minor tackifier-like fraction at matched reactive mass fraction and comparable realized viscosity state.
Include an appropriate reactive-core reference so the observed drift can be compared with the linear-dilution prediction.
Keep the interpretation within the measured 15 to 60 minute window and report the realized viscosity level and temperature support to identify state mismatches.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and matched process state, does a resin-modified composition produce 120 C isothermal drift substantially below the linear reactive-core dilution prediction, and is low drift obtained only when the minor tackifier-like axis is nonzero rather than with the acrylic-like axis alone?

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If the matched-window drift is below half the linear-dilution prediction, approximately below 3.80%, this supports H-RESIN, falsifies H-CORE at the declared resolution, and, because the composition contains no minor tackifier-like modifier, falsifies H-DUAL's requirement that acrylic-only compositions cannot reach the low-drift regime.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If the drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction, approximately 7.61% for the 20% acrylic composition, H-RESIN is falsified and the result supports reactive-core dilution as the dominant explanation; a near-linear result also remains consistent with H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between the low-drift threshold and the linear prediction would indicate partial or unresolved suppression and would not cleanly adjudicate H-CORE versus H-RESIN; H-DUAL would remain unresolved because the acrylic-only result would not establish whether a nonzero minor tackifier is required.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: The 15% acrylic level is within the broad supported region but its external fraction denominator is explicitly provisional, and its smaller intervention gives a less pronounced separation from the E1-based linear prediction.

The dual-axis composition tests a performance-mitigation intervention but cannot determine whether acrylic alone reaches the low-drift regime, so it is weaker for falsifying H-DUAL; it also uses a larger combined modifier burden.

A minor-tackifier-only composition can test whether the tackifier axis is effective, but it does not directly test the acrylic-only branch needed to discriminate the dual-axis specialization hypothesis.

proposer.reasoning: A 20% acrylic-only composition is directly supported by the external evidence, lies within the conservative acrylic intervention band, and retains a simple single-axis attribution. The direct 120 C matched-window hold measures the declared failure coordinate without model fitting. Relative to E1, the reactive-core prediction is approximately 9.51% times 0.80, or 7.61%; the registry's superlinear-suppression criterion is below 3.80%. Thus the experiment can distinguish linear dilution from strong resin suppression while directly testing whether acrylic alone can falsify the tackifier-required specialization hypothesis.

robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: Deterministic VOI ranking and tied top set were withheld, so S1C49::M-HOLD-120 cannot be established as belonging to the deterministic top set. Retaining it is justified by scientific evidence: it directly measures the least-resolved isothermal drift coordinate, uses a supported 20% acrylic-only intervention, and provides causal isolation for H-CORE versus strong acrylic-associated H-RESIN suppression.
residual_decision_risk: H-DUAL remains unresolved unless a matched nonzero-minor-tackifier composition is also tested.
Large preparation-state variability may obscure separation of the 3.80% suppression threshold from the 7.61% linear prediction.
Two repeats without a prespecified aggregation and uncertainty rule do not support sharp falsification decisions.
Unverified modifier functionality may invalidate the reactive-mass-fraction and stoichiometric calculation.
Without a same-campaign reactive-core reference and realized-state control, drift differences may be confounded by process history or viscosity-scale state.
The result supports formulation-level prediction rules only and cannot establish a molecular reaction mechanism.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: S1C49 tests only the acrylic-only branch and cannot adjudicate H-DUAL for all possible outcomes. This does not make the direct matched-window hold scientifically uninformative or require replacing it: it remains the strongest single-axis experiment for distinguishing linear reactive-core dilution from strong acrylic-associated suppression. The proposal must instead state that H-DUAL is only tested on its acrylic-only falsification branch. The objection also requires cautious interpretation because realized-state variability, absent same-campaign controls, unverified modifier functionality, and the lack of a prespecified repeat aggregation rule prevent strong mechanistic or threshold claims.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No recommendation_flip_boundary, top_experiment_set_stability, or base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower was supplied because VOI scoring was withheld. Therefore no specific weight perturbation can be identified or judged defensible; the decision rests on the explicit scientific design evidence rather than reported score stability.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: SI_15_60 is directly measured at 15 and 60 minutes, so the protocol can produce a value above 7.61% or below 3.80%. The criteria are not practically reliable as written because the protocol has only two repeats, does not prescribe an uncertainty or aggregation rule, and does not control the realized state despite the documented large E2 preparation spread. Thus the numerical falsification outcomes are observable, but robust adjudication is not guaranteed.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment cannot support a general claim that all three registered hypotheses were adjudicated; at most it can discriminate strong acrylic-associated suppression from near-linear dilution under favorable state control.
objections.objection: The proposer lists H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL in "hypotheses_separated", but S1C49 tests only the acrylic-only composition (20% acrylic-like modifier, 0% minor tackifier-like modifier). A result at or above the 7.61% linear prediction is explicitly stated to leave H-DUAL unresolved, and an intermediate result also leaves it unresolved. Thus H-DUAL is not separated across the possible outcome space, contrary to "hypotheses_not_separated": [].

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result could be labeled as falsifying H-CORE or H-RESIN even though repeat scatter makes its distance from 3.80% or 7.61% smaller than the effective experimental uncertainty.
objections.objection: The numerical H-CORE/H-RESIN thresholds are nominally separated: 7.61% versus 3.80%, with a declared discrimination threshold of 2%. However, the proposal provides no repeat-level decision rule or uncertainty treatment for the at-least-two-repeat SI_15_60 measurements. A mean near either boundary could not be classified simply from the stated protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A drift below 3.80% could not be attributed specifically to resin-continuum or encounter-frequency suppression beyond dilution; it could instead reflect unaccounted stoichiometry or modifier reactivity. Molecular or functional-group mechanism attribution is unavailable from this experiment.
objections.objection: The 20% acrylic intervention simultaneously changes acrylic-like modifier content and reactive mass fraction from 1.0 to 0.80. The prediction 9.51% x 0.80 = 7.61% accounts for mass dilution, but the protocol does not verify whether the acrylic material contributes reactive OH or other NCO-reactive functionality. The supplied core anchor explicitly states that true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified specifications if the modifier is reactive.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any observed difference from the E1-derived 7.61% prediction could be incorrectly attributed to acrylic chemistry rather than to an unmatched realization state or campaign-level process effect.
objections.objection: The planner requires comparison at matched reactive mass fraction and comparable realized viscosity state, but S1C49 contains only one acrylic-only composition and M-HOLD-120. It does not include a matched minor-tackifier composition, a reactive-core control prepared in the same campaign, or a state-calibration measurement. Therefore the acrylic-axis result cannot distinguish modifier-axis behavior from preparation, thermal-history, or realized-state differences.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The numerical drift estimate remains directly interpretable, but its comparison with the 7.61% reference prediction would not establish the claimed formulation-level mechanism.
objections.objection: SI_15_60 is correctly defined as a directly measured matched-window quantity from eta_15 and eta_60, so it does not inherit the regression-fit weakness of M-SWEEP or the shared-shape assumptions of M-ANCHOR. However, its interpretation as a formulation mechanism still depends on the unmeasured condition that the acrylic composition has a comparable realized viscosity state and thermal history to the E1 reference.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A near-7.61% result could be declared a falsification of H-RESIN even when preparation-state variation dominates the difference from the prediction.
objections.objection: The protocol can directly produce SI_15_60, but the stated falsification rule "at or above 7.61%" for H-RESIN is too sharp for the specified two-repeat design and the known realization variability. The supplied E2 repeats show a 120 C between-preparation max/min ratio of 3.57x, while the M-HOLD-120 protocol specifies only two repeats and no requirement to quantify or beat that state variability.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment may yield an apparent threshold crossing without a defensible basis for accepting H-RESIN or falsifying H-CORE.
objections.objection: The low-drift acceptance threshold of approximately 3.80% is more than 2 percentage points below the 7.61% linear prediction, so it is nominally above the catalog's 2.0% discrimination threshold. The remaining practical problem is not direct observability but lack of a prespecified repeat aggregation and uncertainty criterion; two independent repeats may not establish that the composition is truly below 3.80%.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could be overstated as proving a chemical mechanism rather than discriminating the registered formulation-level prediction rules.
objections.objection: No reliance on the withheld validation formulation identity or outcome is evident. The proposal stays within the registry's formulation-level rheological boundary and does not claim a molecularly resolved reaction pathway. The phrase "reactive-core dilution as the dominant explanation" should nevertheless be limited to consistency with the registered rheological model, because M-HOLD-120 alone cannot establish dominance over all alternative chemistry or process explanations.

skeptic.recommended_change: Revise the claim to state that S1C49 primarily tests H-CORE versus strong acrylic-associated H-RESIN suppression and only tests one falsification branch of H-DUAL. Add a same-campaign reactive-core reference, verify modifier functionality and recalculate stoichiometry, use a state anchor or matched realized-viscosity criterion before the hold, and include a nonzero minor-tackifier composition at the same reactive mass fraction if H-DUAL is to be genuinely adjudicated.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The proposal claims to separate H-DUAL, but S1C49 tests only the acrylic-only branch and explicitly leaves H-DUAL unresolved for at-or-above-linear and intermediate outcomes; therefore its declared hypothesis coverage is false across the possible results. In addition, the protocol does not measure or control the comparable realized viscosity state required by the planner despite documented E2 state variability up to a 3.57x max/min ratio at 120 C.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.
